scenario: A third-party reimbursement against a personal expense (scenario-analysis.md #31, ADR-0008 — this is what 'reimbursement' means now, replacing the previously-undefined Expense.relationship_type value)

original_expense.description: Client dinner while traveling for work

reimbursement_payment.counterparty_hint: Employer payroll/expense system — not modeled as a Person; there is no beneficiary-graph relationship to it

original_allocation_v2.note: Net-zero, resolved the same deterministic way as fixtures/refund-full.json — one line per original beneficiary (here, just Dev), each at amount 0, never an empty lines array (invariants.md #12a).

note: No Obligation and no Settlement anywhere in this fixture — the employer was never a beneficiary in the ledger's graph, so there was never a debt to discharge, only a cost to net out. This is mechanically identical to a merchant_refund (same ExpenseAdjustment table, same netAmount computation, same Allocation-supersession mechanism); only kind and the counterparty differ. Contrast with docs/decisions/0008-refunds-and-reimbursements-as-adjustments.md's comparison table (paid_on_behalf vs merchant_refund vs third_party_reimbursement vs Settlement).
